t: The Kushans, a branch of the Yuezhi, built an empire from Bactria across the Hindu Kush to the Ganges plain in the 1st–2nd centuries.
They controlled Silk Road trade between Han China, Parthia and Rome, and minted abundant gold coins showing gods of many religions.
Under Kanishka the Great, Gandharan and Mathuran art produced early images of the Buddha, and Buddhism spread into Central Asia.
dyk: Kushan coins show a mix of gods, from the Iranian Mithra and the goddess Nana to Shiva, Heracles and the Buddha, labelled in Bactrian as Boddo.
ev: Kujula Kadphises unites the five Yuezhi chiefdoms of Bactria
A Kushan army crossing the Pamirs is repulsed by the Han general Ban Chao
Accession of Kanishka the Great and start of his era
Huvishka succeeds Kanishka; the empire is at its height
An embassy from the Kushan king, probably Vasudeva I, reaches the Wei court
Shapur I claims Kushanshahr as far as Peshawar
Kidarites overrun the last Kushan kingdoms

f.capital: Bactria; later Purushapura (Peshawar), with Mathura and Kapisa as royal centres
f.successor: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom; Kidarite Kingdom; Gupta Empire
